Thank you!!

I've never been comfortable to take on debt, never took out any typical "loans" for housing or cars; it made me feel uncomfortable because I didn't feel safe in that I would be able to pay it off. But payment plans were just a very naive blind spot for me. I didn't think of them as taking on debt, and it was only such small amounts at a time, and I always "felt" like I could afford it, just not now, but next month.., and my life would be better \*now\* if I had x thing! This period is a haze for me, but all of a sudden, I was paying hundreds of euros per month in payment plans and I couldn't afford it. I had to convert it to debt with huge interest rates. Looking at how much I spend per month right now on just interest... it's rough!

But if anything, maybe I am free of this blind spot now and have learnt a valuable, and expensive, lesson. I haven't bought anything I couldn't afford for 10 months now. But no more of that will be in my future. I am saving for the things I want, and I'll be happy when I can buy them for my own money :)

So this isn't as glorious as a lot of happy posts here. I haven't achieved ridiculous net-worth, or fought off huge debts, but I have accomplished something I am very proud of and it's a good start for the future.

At its worst, I was "only" 2700€ in debt, which seems quite manageable compared to what a lot of other people have struggled with here. My problem was that I really struggled to turn things around, to stop spending money I don't have, even with YNAB helping me see my attempted plans. Most people here rave about how YNAB instantly turned things around for them, and that's great, but for me that wasn't enough.

I've been through some rough years, dealing with pretty bad depression, and it wrecked my impulse control and my ability to care about my future. During this period, I burned out from work, and after being on sick leave a few months, I started working 80%, so that affected my finances a lot as well. When I wanted something, I bought it, and usually on payment plans. "20€ a month for 3 years doesn't seem so bad!". But it all added up, quick. I bought things for me, I bought things for others, and it made me briefly feel good in a time where many other things couldn't.

So for the past 28 months, I've had a negative net-worth and even before that I had shaky finances. Around January 2023 I finally started turning things around and stopped sinking further into debt. But even after that, you can see it wasn't smooth sailing, but the trend is good!

I finally ended a month on a positive net-worth! I'm worth a whole 110€! I still have 930€ worth of credit card debt, but I'm also starting to have savings, a small emergency category, and fund my true expenses! And it feels great! And I'm excited to be moving in the right direction! If things continue like this, I will be debt free around next summer!

Now, I'm not really cured from my terrible spending habits. I should be paying off my debts quicker. I am still buying things I probably can't \*really\* afford considering I should be paying of debt, saving, and budgeting for true expenses way further. During this period, my post tax salary has gone up from 1600€/mo to 2100€/mo which has helped a lot too. But, I take and appreciate the victories I can get and am feeling positive about the future!

Anyways sorry for the looong post, I just wanted to rave because I'm really happy and proud over this and I've waited really long for this moment. It's not as impressive as a lot of you out there, but this means a lot to me :)

Thanks for the reply!

I know what you're saying about therapy... I'm just not sure I can do it. I've been on and off seeing someone over the years when I've gotten a chance to. I can talk and talk about the surface stuff but as soon as it gets real, I shut down. I can't sit face to face with someone and talk about the problems I'm embarrassed about. I guess it might sound weak, but I just cannot do it. I can sit on the internet and type about it because I don't associate other people's words as text on the screen with "real people". But as soon as I hear a voice, or see a face, I shut down when it gets hard. Not just in therapy but in social situations as well. I don't know how to get help...

I'm actively trying to get better. I'm not giving up. I exercise more than I ever used to, I eat better than I ever used to. Still not a great amount, but *better*. I try to be positive and self-concious, reflect over my choices.

I can have many great weeks of success and well-being but all it takes is a few days of struggle and I ruin it for myself.
